extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums (Stack Exchange), it contains 64,696 VQAs with authentic context, answers validated by those who asked the questions, and user-chosen topics from 105 diverse topics spanning five super-categories. A critical distinction is its lengthy answers (mean of 173 words), which necessitates a new evaluation methodology compared to standard VQA datasets.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari
extraction.publisher: University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder
extraction.inLanguage: English (and multilingual content from Stack Exchange communities)
extraction.citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., & Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4 [cs.CV].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected by scraping the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange. The publicly-available data spanned from August 2010 to November 2022, adhering to all data license restrictions (cc-by-sa 4.0). From the Stack Exchange archive, all examples containing four components were collected: a natural language question, a natural language context, an image, and at least one answer. The natural language question was collected as the post 'title', the image as a URL link, the natural language context via a 'body' text entry field, and answers were publicly provided by individuals on the site. Only examples where the question poster marked an 'accepted answer' were used.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some visual questions were excluded because the image could not be downloaded from the provided URL link, reducing the dataset from 65,849 to 64,696 visual questions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Stack Exchange online question-answering platform archive, hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format. The initial pool started with 330,705 candidate visual questions from 105 topical sites belonging to five super-categories (culture & recreation, life & arts, science, professional, and business).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For data format consistency, all images were converted to PNG format. Dataset splits were created by randomly selecting from each of the 105 topics 7 examples for training and 3 examples for validation for topics with at least 20 examples, resulting in training (665), validation (285), and test (63,746) splits.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two filtering steps were applied: (1) Removed visual questions without an accepted answer (330,705 reduced to 165,766). (2) Removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer (reduced to 119,177). (3) Removed visual questions with multiple images or GIFs (reduced to 85,573). (4) Removed visual questions with visual answers (reduced to 65,849). (5) Removed examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided link (final dataset: 64,696). All images were converted to PNG format. Technology topics (75 topics, e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) were excluded because they typically involve language problems about code shown in screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two types of annotations were collected: (1) User intention annotations: Three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk annotated the intent for 105 examples (one from each topic). Two independent workers (A and B) annotated each VQA instance. For 25 out of 105 cases where annotations did not match, a third worker (C) broke the tie. The final label used majority vote from 3 crowdsourced labels per visual question. (2) Human quality judgments: Ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic) were hired for an IRB-approved human study. Each expert was assigned 20 VQAs on their topic and asked to rate six model-generated answers per VQA as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1). A home-grown, web-based interface was used. Additionally, two authors performed multi-round annotation (4 rounds on 105 visual questions total) to develop and refine the user intention taxonomy.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intention annotations); home-grown web-based interface (for domain expert quality judgments). Code available at https://github.com/VQAonline/VQAonlineVisualization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two annotators (authors) tagged categories for visual questions across four rounds, resolving disagreements through discussion. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69% across rounds. For crowdworker annotations, when two workers disagreed (25 out of 105 cases), a third worker broke the tie. For domain expert evaluations, Pearson and Spearman correlations between evaluation metrics and human judgments were computed to assess metric alignment with human assessments.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: User intention: 2 primary annotations per VQA (with a 3rd tiebreaker for disagreements, i.e., majority vote from 3 labels). Domain expert quality judgment: 1 annotation per model-generated answer per VQA (6 model answers rated per VQA, totaling 1200 human judgments for 200 VQAs).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers (user intention): Located in the United States, completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over 95% approval rating. Domain experts (quality judgment): Ten individuals, each a domain expert in one of ten topics (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, and Artificial Intelligence), each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic, located in the United States (to guarantee English proficiency).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: DeepSolo (state-of-the-art text spotter model) was used to detect text presence in all images in the dataset, finding that 76% (48,161 images) contain text. LLaMA2 was used as an automated evaluation metric to rate model-generated answers.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly shared at https://vqaonline.github.io/. No explicit versioning, update schedule, or deprecation policy is described in the paper.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains user-generated content from Stack Exchange users, which may include personal opinions, experiences, and information shared publicly by users. The dataset includes multilingual content from users across various countries. No explicit collection of demographic attributes (e.g., gender, age) is described.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improved models designed for VQAonline can benefit many real-world applications including other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing. The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more representation from countries like the US, India, and Europe and less from countries like Egypt.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more from countries like US, India, Europe and less from countries like Egypt. Models trained on Stack Exchange data may have an unfair advantage when evaluated on this dataset. The dataset has a long-tail distribution across different topics, with as few as 10 examples in some topics and over 20,000 in others. 52% of all VQAs belong to only 23% of the topics (24 science topics).
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The mainstream VQA evaluation metric is ill-suited for the dataset's lengthy textual answers (mean 173 words). The dataset may not generalize well to populations without internet access or mobile devices. Some models evaluated may have been trained on Stack Exchange data, creating potential data contamination. The dataset excludes 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) because they typically involve language problems about code in screenshots. The geographic and socioeconomic representation is skewed toward users with internet access in certain countries.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for: (1) Benchmarking and testing VQA models, particularly large Vision and Language Models (VLMs) in zero-shot and few-shot settings; (2) Training and fine-tuning VQA models for authentic, long-form answer generation; (3) Evaluation metric research for long-form text in VQA; (4) Research on user intention classification in visual question answering; (5) Multilingual VQA research; (6) Research on hallucination issues in VLMs in authentic use cases. The dataset supports few-shot learning with training (665), validation (285), and test (63,746) splits.
